rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A is about missing try/catch around image fetching in pptx-actions.ts causing full export failure; Finding B is a documentation markdown line-wrap readability nit in themes-and-layouts.md. Entirely unrelated files and defects.

panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts::pptx export aborts entirely when a single image fetch fails, unlike the pdf path which degrades gracefully
panel.summary: PPTX export aborts entirely when a single image fetch fails, unlike the PDF path which degrades gracefully
panel.evidence: `fetchImage: async (src) => { const blob = await docsImageFetcher(src); ... }` has no try/catch. `docsImageFetcher` throws on any non-ok response (export-utils.ts:52-54), and `exportPptx` awaits it inside its media loop (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162) with no error handling, so one deleted/403/404 image src rejects the whole export and the user gets `Export failed: Image fetch failed: 404 ...` and no file. The sibling PDF path deliberately swallows per-image failures and substitutes BLANK_PNG (packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:277-283), so behavior is inconsistent and a single broken image makes the deck un-exportable to PPTX.
